Alban Isidor Stolz was a German Catholic theologian and widely read religious author, born at Bühl in Baden in 1808 and dead at Freiburg in 1883. After studying law briefly, he turned to theology at Freiburg, passed through a period of doubt, and regained his faith while studying language and literature at Heidelberg. He then entered the seminary at Freiburg to prepare for the priesthood.

Stolz won lasting fame as a writer of popular religious books rather than as a scholar. His command of language and his eye for human nature set his work apart. His Legende, a book of saints' legends called the Christian starry heaven, ran through many editions, and his short moral and argumentative pieces were gathered as Kleinigkeiten. His collected works filled nineteen volumes, published at Freiburg between 1871 and 1895.
